hi.title: घरेलू हिंसा से महिलाओं का संरक्षण अधिनियम, 2005
hi.summary: यह अधिनियम महिलाओं को परिवार के भीतर होने वाली घरेलू हिंसा से प्रभावी कानूनी संरक्षण प्रदान करने के लिए बनाया गया है और पूरे भारत में लागू है।

question: What is the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005?
answer: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 provides legal protection to women who are victims of domestic violence. It extends to the whole of India and came into force on a date notified by the Central Government.

hi.title: पीड़ित महिला की परिभाषा

question: Who is an aggrieved person under this Act?
answer: An aggrieved person means any woman who is, or has been, in a domestic relationship with the respondent and who alleges that she has been subjected to any act of domestic violence by the respondent.

hi.title: घरेलू संबंध
hi.summary: घरेलू संबंध वह संबंध है जिसमें दो व्यक्ति साझा घर में साथ रहते हैं या रह चुके हैं और वे विवाह, रक्त संबंध, गोद लेने या संयुक्त परिवार से जुड़े हों।

question: What is a domestic relationship under this Act?
answer: A domestic relationship means a relationship between two persons who live or have lived together in a shared household and are related by consanguinity, marriage, a relationship in the nature of marriage, adoption, or as members of a joint family.

question: What is a shared household under this Act?
answer: A shared household means a household where the aggrieved person lives or has lived in a domestic relationship with the respondent. It includes jointly or separately owned or tenanted property and may also include a joint family household.

question: What constitutes domestic violence under this Act?
answer: Domestic violence includes any act, omission or conduct that harms or endangers the health, safety, life or well-being of the aggrieved person. It includes physical abuse, sexual abuse, verbal and emotional abuse, economic abuse, dowry-related harassment, threats and other conduct causing physical or mental harm.

question: Who can report domestic violence under this Act?
answer: Any person who has reason to believe that an act of domestic violence has been, is being, or is likely to be committed may provide information to the concerned Protection Officer. No civil or criminal liability is incurred for giving such information in good faith.

question: What information must be given to an aggrieved woman after a domestic violence complaint?
answer: The aggrieved woman must be informed about her right to seek protection orders, residence orders, monetary relief, custody orders, compensation orders, the availability of service providers, Protection Officers, free legal services and, wherever relevant, her right to file a complaint under section 498A of the Indian Penal Code.

question: Can an aggrieved woman seek shelter under this Act?
answer: Yes. If an aggrieved woman, or a Protection Officer or service provider on her behalf, requests shelter, the person in charge of the shelter home shall provide shelter to the aggrieved woman.

question: Who appoints Protection Officers under this Act?
answer: The State Government appoints the required number of Protection Officers for each district and notifies the area in which they exercise their powers. As far as possible, Protection Officers shall be women.

question: What are the main duties of a Protection Officer?
answer: A Protection Officer assists the Magistrate, prepares domestic incident reports, helps file applications for relief, ensures legal aid, maintains lists of service providers, arranges shelter and medical examination when required, and helps execute monetary relief orders.

answer: A registered service provider may record a domestic incident report, arrange medical examination, help provide shelter to the aggrieved woman, and forward the required reports to the Protection Officer, Magistrate and police as provided under the Act.

question: Does a woman have the right to live in the shared household?
answer: Yes. Every woman in a domestic relationship has the right to reside in the shared household, whether or not she has any right, title or beneficial interest in it. She cannot be evicted or excluded except in accordance with the procedure established by law.

question: What is a protection order under this Act?
answer: After giving both parties an opportunity of being heard and being prima facie satisfied that domestic violence has taken place or is likely to take place, the Magistrate may pass a protection order prohibiting the respondent from committing or aiding domestic violence and from other specified acts.

question: What residence orders can the Magistrate pass?
answer: The Magistrate may restrain the respondent from dispossessing the aggrieved person, direct the respondent to remove himself from the shared household, restrict entry into portions of the household, prevent disposal of the shared household, or direct alternate accommodation or payment of rent, as provided under the Act.

question: What monetary relief can be granted under this Act?
answer: The Magistrate may direct the respondent to pay monetary relief for expenses and losses suffered due to domestic violence, including loss of earnings, medical expenses, property damage, and maintenance for the aggrieved person and her children. question: Can the Magistrate grant child custody under this Act?
answer: Yes. At any stage of the proceedings, the Magistrate may grant temporary custody of a child to the aggrieved person or the person applying on her behalf and may specify arrangements for visitation. If visitation may harm the child, it may be refused.

hi.title: आदेश की निःशुल्क प्रति
hi.summary: मजिस्ट्रेट अधिनियम के अंतर्गत पारित आदेश की प्रति संबंधित पक्षों, पुलिस तथा सेवा प्रदाता को निःशुल्क उपलब्ध कराएगा।

question: Are copies of court orders provided free of cost?
answer: Yes. The Magistrate shall provide copies of every order passed under the Act free of cost to the parties, the police officer in charge of the concerned police station and the relevant service provider.
source: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005

hi.title: आदेश की अवधि एवं संशोधन
hi.summary: संरक्षण आदेश तब तक प्रभावी रहता है जब तक पीड़ित महिला उसके निरसन का आवेदन न करे। परिस्थितियों में परिवर्तन होने पर मजिस्ट्रेट आदेश में संशोधन या निरस्तीकरण कर सकता है।

question: Can a protection order be modified or revoked?
answer: Yes. A protection order remains in force until the aggrieved person applies for its discharge. If circumstances change, the Magistrate may alter, modify or revoke the order after recording reasons in writing.
source: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005

hi.title: अन्य न्यायिक कार्यवाहियों में राहत
hi.summary: अधिनियम के अंतर्गत उपलब्ध राहतें दीवानी, पारिवारिक अथवा आपराधिक न्यायालय की अन्य कार्यवाहियों में भी मांगी जा सकती हैं।

question: Can relief under this Act be claimed in other court proceedings?
answer: Yes. Reliefs available under sections 18, 19, 20, 21 and 22 may also be sought in proceedings before a civil court, family court or criminal court, in addition to any other relief available under law.

hi.title: क्षेत्राधिकार
hi.summary: पीड़ित महिला जहां रहती है, कार्य करती है, प्रतिवादी रहता है या जहां घटना हुई है, वहां का सक्षम मजिस्ट्रेट इस अधिनियम के अंतर्गत मामलों की सुनवाई कर सकता है।

question: Which court has jurisdiction under this Act?
answer: The Judicial Magistrate of the First Class or Metropolitan Magistrate within whose jurisdiction the aggrieved person resides, works, the respondent resides or works, or where the cause of action arose, is competent to grant relief under this Act. Orders are enforceable throughout India.

hi.title: संरक्षण आदेश के उल्लंघन की सजा
hi.summary: संरक्षण आदेश या अंतरिम संरक्षण आदेश का उल्लंघन अपराध है, जिसके लिए एक वर्ष तक का कारावास, बीस हजार रुपये तक का जुर्माना या दोनों हो सकते हैं।

question: What is the punishment for violating a protection order?
answer: A breach of a protection order or interim protection order is an offence punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to twenty thousand rupees, or with both.
source: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
